SAMSUNG IS DEVELOPING GAIA, AN AI ACCELERATOR FOR AI PCS.

THE COMPANY HAS ALREADY SUPPLIED PROTOTYPES TO MAJOR CUSTOMERS SUCH AS CHINA’S LENOVO AND U.S.-BASED HP FOR PERFORMANCE VALIDATION.

MASS PRODUCTION COULD BEGIN AS EARLY AS NEXT YEAR. THE CHIP WILL BE MANUFACTURED ON A 4NM PROCESS.

SAMSUNG IS ALSO PUSHING TO INTEGRATE IT WITH PROCESSING-IN-MEMORY, OR PIM, A NEXT-GENERATION DRAM TECHNOLOGY CAPABLE OF PERFORMING COMPUTATIONS ON STORED DATA ITSELF.

UNLIKE CONVENTIONAL PROCESSORS THAT SERVE AS THE BRAIN OF A PC, GAIA IS SPECIALIZED FOR AI COMPUTATION. IT IS DESIGNED WITH AN OPTIMIZED NEURAL PROCESSING UNIT, OR NPU, ARCHITECTURE TO EFFICIENTLY HANDLE GENERATIVE AI TASKS ON PCS.
